items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Advanced degree in related area, such as a Juris Doctor. (Required)
Experience practicing civil law (litigation and or legislation/policy).
Demonstrated ability to collaborate and work effectively with individuals and groups from a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.

The Staff Attorney - Anti-Corruption supports substantive legal work for the Edley Center on Law & Democracy. This position exists because the Center engages in a wide range of legal research and advocacy that requires dedicated attorneys with civil litigation and policy experience. The Staff Attorney may work on state and local policy development in California as well as other states, amicus briefs, impact litigation, delivering on MOUs with government agencies, providing legal guidance to community partners and coalitions, and more.
Supports Center cases and projects at the direction of the Executive Director.
Conducts legal research and writing on cases and projects that fall within the scope and focus of the Edley Center, routinely focusing on state authorities and countering public corruption.
Drafts and files amicus briefs, motions and other materials on a wide range of topics.
Mentorship and Coalition Coordination
Mentors and works with student intern researchers to provide feedback and manage projects.
Consults with coalition partners to meet litigation filing deadlines and policy deadlines.
Meets and consults with potential clients to file amicus briefs, offer advice memos, or training materials.
Liaises with Center partners and/or other stakeholders as necessary in order to gather information necessary to move litigation or policy projects forward.
Case Investigation and Development
Assists with case investigation and development:
Reviews and analyzes pending and enacted legislation.
Assists in determining scope, timing and direction of the investigations.
Reviews case records and filings, and analyze options.
Makes court appearances as needed.
Performs additional duties as assigned.
Expertise in legal research, analysis, and advocacy strategy development.
A member in good standing of the CA Bar Association. (Required)
Proven abilities in collaboration, facilitation, and strategic and creative thinking.
Thorough understanding of complex legal issues.
Demonstrated commitment to the highest ethical standards.
Strong attention to detail.
Demonstrated commitment to fostering an inclusive and supportive environment that promotes collaboration and mutual respect among all members of the UC Berkeley community and its stakeholders.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills to communicate effectively with all levels of staff and influence, both verbally and in writing.
Advanced knowledge in civil or criminal law related to corruption.
Ability to exercise sound judgement, use discretion and maintain all confidentiality.
Advanced project management and organizational skills.
Ability to multi-task with demanding timeframes.
Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop creative and
In-depth research skills to draft accurate, complete and persuasive legal documents, such as pleadings, legal responses, affidavits, position statements and briefs.

Computer and technical skills, including proficiency in using standard productivity, communication, and video conferencing platforms (e.g., Microsoft Office Suite, Google Workspace, Zoom); ability to learn and effectively use new software systems and digital tools as required to meet evolving program needs.

Must demonstrate strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to engage with and understand individuals from varied academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender, and ethnic backgrounds.
